summary: A lobed deciduous tree leaf often known for bright autumn color.
fun_facts: Sugar maple sap is boiled down to make maple syrup.
The leaves usually have five main lobes.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Wilted maple leaves can be hazardous to some animals.
habitat: Cool deciduous forests, parks, and mature yards.

summary: A long-lived oak with rounded leaf lobes and acorns.
fun_facts: White oak wood is valued for barrels and furniture.
Mature trees can support many insects and birds.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Acorns and leaves contain tannins that may irritate people or animals.
habitat: Dry upland forests, mixed woods, and open savannas.

summary: A low-growing plant with yellow composite flowers and puffball seed heads.
fun_facts: The seed head acts like a tiny parachute system.
Dandelions can bloom repeatedly through the growing season.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Some people may react to the sap or to contaminated plants.
habitat: Lawns, meadows, sidewalks, gardens, and disturbed soil.

summary: A tall annual with a large composite flower head and broad leaves.
fun_facts: The flower head is made of many smaller florets.
Young flower heads can track the sun before flowering.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Plant parts can cause reactions in sensitive people or animals.
habitat: Open fields, gardens, roadsides, and disturbed soil.

summary: A woody flowering shrub with layered petals and often thorny stems.
fun_facts: Rose hips are the fruit of rose plants.
There are thousands of cultivated rose varieties.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Thorns can puncture skin and treated garden plants may carry chemicals.
habitat: Gardens, hedges, woodland edges, and sunny shrub borders.

summary: A fragrant shrubby herb with narrow leaves and purple flower spikes.
fun_facts: Lavender oil is widely used in fragrance products.
The plant prefers sunny, well-drained sites.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Concentrated oils and plant parts can bother pets or sensitive people.
habitat: Sunny gardens, dry slopes, herb beds, and Mediterranean-style landscapes.

summary: A small pale mushroom with a rounded cap and gills underneath.
fun_facts: Cremini and portobello mushrooms are mature forms of the same species.
Wild Agaricus species can be difficult to separate by sight.
toxicity_note: Do not eat mushrooms identified by this app. Mushroom lookalikes may be hazardous or deadly.
habitat: Cultivated beds, compost-rich soils, lawns, and grassy areas.

summary: A striking mushroom often showing a red cap with pale warts.
fun_facts: It forms partnerships with tree roots.
Cap color can vary from red to orange or yellowish.
toxicity_note: Do not eat mushrooms identified by this app. This mushroom can contain psychoactive and toxic compounds.
origin: Fruiting body of a mycorrhizal fungus
habitat: Woodlands and forest edges near birch, pine, spruce, and other trees.
regions: Introduced in parts of the Southern Hemisphere

summary: A golden funnel-shaped mushroom group with ridges that can resemble gills.
fun_facts: Many chanterelles grow in partnership with trees.
False chanterelles can look similar in casual photos.
toxicity_note: Do not eat mushrooms identified by this app. Similar-looking mushrooms can be harmful.
habitat: Mossy forests, hardwood stands, conifer woods, and damp woodland floors.

summary: A soft moss group that forms dense mats in bogs and wetlands.
fun_facts: Sphagnum can hold many times its weight in water.
Accumulated sphagnum material can become peat.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Wetland moss can host microbes or environmental contaminants.
habitat: Bogs, fens, wet forests, seepage slopes, and acidic wetlands.

summary: A fine-textured turf grass that forms dense lawns and meadows.
fun_facts: It spreads by underground rhizomes.
Its seed head has a loose pyramid shape.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Lawn grasses may be treated with chemicals.
habitat: Lawns, pastures, meadows, roadsides, and open fields.

summary: A bramble fruit made of clustered drupelets on thorny canes.
fun_facts: Blackberries are aggregates of many tiny fruits.
Many species spread quickly through canes and seeds.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Wild berries can have dangerous lookalikes or contamination.
habitat: Hedgerows, woodland edges, fields, disturbed sites, and sunny thickets.

summary: A climbing or trailing plant with three leaflets that can cause skin irritation.
fun_facts: The irritating oil can persist on tools and clothing.
It can grow as a vine, shrub, or groundcover.
toxicity_note: Avoid touching suspected poison ivy. It can cause serious skin reactions in many people.
habitat: Woodland edges, trails, fences, yards, and disturbed ground.

summary: A fleshy rosette-forming succulent with thick lance-shaped leaves.
fun_facts: Aloe leaves store water in gel-filled tissue.
It is commonly grown as a houseplant.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Aloe latex and plant parts can bother people and pets.
habitat: Dry gardens, containers, sunny windows, and arid landscapes.

summary: A cactus with flattened pads, spines, and sometimes colorful fruit.
fun_facts: Tiny glochid spines can detach easily.
Many species have bright yellow, orange, or pink flowers.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Spines and glochids can injure skin, eyes, or pets.
habitat: Deserts, dry grasslands, rocky slopes, and xeric gardens.

summary: An aquatic plant with round leaves and large flowers held above the water.
fun_facts: Lotus leaves are famous for repelling water.
The seed pods have a distinctive flat-topped shape.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Aquatic plants can absorb pollutants from water.
habitat: Ponds, lakes, slow wetlands, and cultivated water gardens.

summary: A wetland plant with tall strap-like leaves and brown cylindrical flower spikes.
fun_facts: Cattails help provide cover for wetland wildlife.
The fluffy seed material disperses on wind.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Wetland plants can accumulate pollutants.
habitat: Marshes, pond edges, ditches, and shallow wetlands.

summary: A round tree fruit with smooth skin and a central core.
fun_facts: Apple trees are commonly grafted to preserve varieties.
There are thousands of named apple cultivars.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Seeds contain compounds of concern and wild fruit can be contaminated.
habitat: Orchards, gardens, temperate farms, and abandoned homesteads.

summary: A woody cone that protects and releases pine seeds.
fun_facts: Many pine cones open and close with humidity.
Some species release seeds after fire.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Cones can carry sap, mold, insects, or environmental contaminants.
habitat: Conifer forests, parks, mountains, sandy soils, and plantations.

summary: A fern with arching fronds made of many small leaflets.
fun_facts: Ferns reproduce with spores rather than flowers.
Boston fern is a common hanging houseplant.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Houseplants may be treated with chemicals or confused with irritating species.
habitat: Humid forests, shaded gardens, containers, and indoor spaces.

summary: A tropical climbing plant with large split or perforated leaves.
fun_facts: Leaf holes are called fenestrations.
It climbs trees in tropical forests.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Monstera contains irritating calcium oxalate crystals.
habitat: Tropical forests, indoor containers, greenhouses, and shaded gardens.

summary: A soft round fruit that grows on a leafy vine-like plant.
fun_facts: Tomatoes are botanically fruits.
Cultivars range from tiny currant tomatoes to large beefsteaks.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Tomato foliage and unripe parts can contain irritating compounds.
habitat: Gardens, farms, containers, and greenhouses.

summary: The nut-like seed of an oak tree, usually held in a small cap.
fun_facts: Acorns are an important food source for wildlife.
The cap shape can help identify the oak group.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Acorns contain tannins and may irritate people or animals.
habitat: Oak forests, parks, yards, and woodland edges.

summary: A creeping plant with three-part leaves and rounded white flower heads.
fun_facts: Clover can fix nitrogen through root bacteria.
Four-leaf forms are uncommon mutations.
toxicity_note: Do not consume based on AI identification. Plants from lawns or fields may carry chemicals or contaminants.
habitat: Lawns, pastures, meadows, roadsides, and open disturbed soil.
